finding.claim: GET /users returns the id and name of every user in whatever org the caller names. The org comes from the query string and is never compared to the caller's own org or identity. The file registers no authentication or authorization middleware, so any client can enumerate any tenant's users (IDOR / broken access control). Severity depends on whether auth middleware that sets req.pg also scopes the org; none is visible in this repo. The query itself is parameterized, so there is no SQL injection.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP client, query parameter ?org=<any org id>
finding.sink: req.pg.query('SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1', [req.query.org])

trace.note: Route /users is registered with no auth or authorization middleware in this file
req.query.org is used directly as the tenant filter
Matching rows are returned to the caller as JSON

finding.guards_checked: No app.use() middleware, session or user check, or org-membership comparison exists in db.js. The query is parameterized with $1, so SQL injection is ruled out. The only file in the directory is db.js, so any external middleware could not be inspected. Also checked and found safe: /file (path.resolve plus a startsWith(ROOT + sep) check blocks traversal) and /count (execFile with fixed arguments, no user input).

verdict.guard_found: none (the query is parameterized at db.js:9, which stops SQL injection but not cross-tenant access)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth middleware and queries `WHERE org = $1` using the caller-supplied req.query.org (db.js:9). Nothing in db.js compares the org to the caller's identity, and the app is not exported, so no outside code can add middleware. Caveat: no app.use() sets req.pg, so as written the route would throw. The file looks like a fragment.

verdict_facts.reason: db.js:8-10 registers /users with no auth check or identity comparison, and db.js:9 filters only by the client-supplied req.query.org (parameterized, so no SQLi), so any HTTP client can list any org's users.
